title: Exact scalar restriction preserves intrinsic completeness
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E and F of Q_l with a specified Q_l-algebra embedding i : E → F, and an arbitrary scheme W, let c be their residue-normalized completed coefficient map [lem-pbc-scalar-tensor-construction]. If K in the F ambient derived category is intrinsically complete [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], then its exact derived restriction along c [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] is intrinsically complete for the E datum. No scalar/completion isomorphism, constructibility or geometric bounds are assumed.

source.place: Tags 099B and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; the concrete finite-free scalar argument of lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-completion-transport, steps 2--3 (agent specialization).

proof.text: The scalar map respects constant sections by its residue normalization. The source uniformizer therefore maps to a unit times a positive power of the target uniformizer. The unit-power criterion identifies completeness for the target uniformizer with completeness for this image, including on every slice.

Exact scalar restriction identifies the augmented Koszul completion computation for the image parameter with that for the source parameter and detects acyclicity. Use the flat scalar Koszul tower restriction comparison and the coefficient presentation comparison with Cech completion to translate the previous completeness statement to the actual intrinsic predicate on the restricted object. This uses only restriction and its unit comparison, not existence of the scalar/completion isomorphism being constructed.

lean.statement:
theorem pbcScalarRestrictionComplete (K : PbcCompletedDerived W (pbcIntegralDatum l F))
    (hK : PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete W (pbcIntegralDatum l F) K) :
    PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete W (pbcIntegralDatum l E)
      ((pbcDerivedRestrict (pbcScalarCoefficientMap l E F i W)).obj K)
